title: SemanticContextResult
description: The machine-readable form of one `Semantic code context` section produced for one coding job. Either the section was injected with bounded, deduplicated, in-scope hits, or it fell back to exact search with an explicit trigger. There is no third state and no partial state. A healthy, current index that legitimately yields nothing is a fallback with trigger `no_context` (design decision D14), never an injected section with an empty `hits` array.

consumer.description: Which coding job requested the section, e.g. `implement-feature`. Distinct per consumer so ri-13 can evaluate injection value per job type.

requested_revision.description: Full Git object ID of HEAD in the agent's own worktree. Present on fallback too — it is what the fallback was requested for.

hits.description: Retained hits in final rendered order (the deterministic rank order of design decision D5).

omissions.description: Every hit the service returned but the section did not render, with the single reason that excluded it. Present on fallback as an empty array.

file_path.description: Repository-relative, normalized path — the same guarantee the rendered hits carry, because an omission names a file too.

reason.description: The first failing check in the fixed evaluation order, so the reason is a function of the inputs alone.

provenance.description: Which index answered and under what authority. Present only when status is `injected`.

index_id.description: Identity of the index that answered. Pinned by `pattern` as well as `format`, which validators ignore by default.

scope_authority.description: Mirrors ri-03's `ScopeDisposition.authority`. `principal_grant` today, because ri-12 sends an explicit scope.

fallback.description: Why no semantic context was injected and what to do instead. Present only when status is `fallback`.

trigger.description: The five triggers: the four of design decision D8 plus `no_context` from D14. `no_context` is the only one that reports a healthy, current index — the query succeeded and the section still has nothing to show.

reason.description: The specific cause. Distinct per cause so the fallback tests can assert exactly, rather than only on the trigger. `index_returned_no_hits` means the index held nothing similar enough inside the declared scope; `all_hits_omitted` means it returned hits and this client's own dedup/budget selection retained none of them. Those are different facts, and only the second one could have been changed by a larger budget.

strategy.description: Matches ri-03's `Fallback.strategy`. Exact search plus direct source reading is the only fallback.

service_state.description: The coordinator's `CodeSearchState`, when a query was actually issued. Absent when a local precondition short-circuited before the call.

allOf.title: A relevance reason belongs to the relevance trigger
allOf.description: Without this, `unavailable` / `index_returned_no_hits` would re-create the defect D14 removed, in the opposite direction: a working service filed under a broken one.

allOf.title: no_context admits only the two relevance reasons
no_context is only reachable from a ready service state
allOf.description: The trigger asserts the service answered and answered well, so the state it answered with is not optional here. A `no_context` emitted from a path that never queried would be an unfalsifiable claim.
